Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

[Object] To provide a molding with an integrated electrode pattern in which a band-shaped second film including an electric connecting portion to be connected to an external substrate can be securely fixed to an inner surface of a resin molded body, and to provide a method for manufacturing the molding with an integrated electrode pattern. [Solution] A molding with an integrated electrode pattern includes a resin molded body; a first film 11 that is formed on an inner surface of the resin molded body and that includes an electrode pattern 13 and a first lead-out wire 63 electrically connected to the electrode pattern; and a second film 4 that is band-shaped, that stands on the inner surface of the resin molded body, and that includes a second lead-out wire 15 electrically connected to the first lead-out wire. The resin molded body includes a pair of support wall portions 3 formed integrally with the inner surface of the resin molded body so as to stand on the inner surface of the resin molded body and clamp both ends of a base part 4a of the second film.

A first film is disposed on the inner surface of the molded body and includes both the electrode pattern and a first lead-out wire. A band-shaped second film extends upright from the inner surface and includes a second lead-out wire that is electrically connected to the first lead-out wire. outputs.L4:
A resin molded body includes a first film provided with a predetermined electrode pattern and a band-shaped second film for electrically connecting the electrode pattern to an external substrate. The first film is integrated with the resin molded body during molding so that the electrode pattern is positioned at a desired location on the molded body. The second film is connected to the first film and extends from the inner surface of the resin molded body in an upright manner. A plurality of lead-out wires formed on the second film are electrically linked to corresponding conductors of the electrode pattern and terminate at a connection portion configured for connection to the external substrate.

To stabilize the second film, the resin molded body is formed with a pair of support walls on its inner surface. The support walls are molded integrally with the resin molded body and arranged on opposite sides of the base portion of the second film. The base portion is therefore clamped between the support walls, restricting displacement, tilting, and bending of the second film. The support walls may extend along at least part of the width of the second film and support the film near the point at which it rises from the molded body.

This arrangement allows the second film to maintain a prescribed orientation and position during subsequent assembly. As a result, the connection portion and the lead-out wires can be accurately aligned with terminals on the external substrate. Loads applied during handling, substrate attachment, or operation are also less likely to concentrate at the junction between the first and second films. The integral support structure thus securely fixes the upright second film without requiring a separate retaining component, simplifies assembly, and improves the mechanical durability and electrical reliability of the connection between the electrode pattern and the external substrate.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise patent abstract for an invention in which a band-shaped connector film is secured inside a resin molded body by integrally formed support walls.
counterfactuals.output: A resin molded body includes an embedded band-shaped connector film having conductive paths extending along its length. Support walls are integrally formed with the molded body on opposing sides of, and optionally through or over, portions of the connector film to retain the film in a predetermined position during and after molding. The support walls suppress displacement, deformation, and separation of the connector film without requiring separate fastening members, thereby improving molding accuracy, electrical connection reliability, and structural durability while enabling a compact component configuration.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the technical problem and proposed structure of a molding that integrates an electrode film, lead-out wires, and a second film for connection to an external substrate.
counterfactuals.output:
The technical problem is to provide a resin molding with a built-in electrode while allowing reliable electrical connection to an external circuit board. If the electrode film itself is extended outside the molded body, its lead-out portion can be displaced, damaged, or subjected to molding pressure and heat; it can also complicate molding and external connection.

The proposed molding therefore includes:

- a molded resin body;
- a first, electrode-bearing film integrated with the body;
- conductive lead-out wires extending from the electrode to a connection region; and
- a separate second film electrically connected to the lead-out wires.

The second film is partly fixed in or to the molding and has an exposed or projecting portion that serves as the connection interface to an external substrate. Thus, the first film performs the sensing/electrode function, while the second film acts as a flexible connection tail, providing a compact, robust electrical path from the embedded electrode to the external circuit board.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
